title: Congress and the White House before 2017
notes: The 1966 hearing, the Church Committee, Schiff's 1994 GAO request and the Rockefeller Initiative. Canon 10 (Goldwater and LeMay) extends it.

lead.text: Before 2017 Congress and the White House touched the subject in a few dated episodes: a one-day House Armed Services hearing in April 1966 followed by an Air Force contract with the University of Colorado, Representative Steven Schiff's request that produced GAO's 1995 Roswell records report, and a privately funded effort in the 1990s to persuade President Clinton to declassify.

summary.text: In late March 1966 House Minority Leader Gerald Ford called for hearings after the Michigan sightings and the swamp gas explanation, and the House Armed Services Committee held a hearing on 5 April 1966; a second proceeding, a House Science and Astronautics symposium, followed in July 1968.

The Church Committee of 1975 and 1976, a select committee of the Senate, investigated the intelligence agencies and recommended the permanent oversight committee that followed it; its own report records how far the agencies controlled what it saw.
GAO, the legislature's auditor, reported to Congress on special access programmes in 1986 and 1988 and on the Roswell records in 1995.

On the White House side, the Rockefeller Initiative of 1993 to 1996 and John Podesta's later public calls are what the record holds; the Clinton Library's UFO files consist of outside correspondence rather than programme records.

record.text: Six months after the 1966 hearing the Air Force let contract 44620-67-C-0035 to the University of Colorado, on 6 October 1966.

Before the contract was let, project coordinator Robert Low wrote on 9 August 1966 that the trick would be to make the project appear totally objective to the public while presenting the image of nonbelievers to scientists. In January 1967 the Air Force's Lt Col Robert Hippler wrote to Condon about seeing whether the Air Force could get out from under the programme.
The Air Force cited the Colorado study and a National Academy of Sciences review as its basis for terminating Project Blue Book on 17 December 1969.

The Church Committee, created by Senate Resolution 21 on 27 January 1975 and chaired by Frank Church, conducted more than 800 interviews and reviewed over 110,000 pages; it reported that in no instance had it been able to examine the agencies' files on its own and that the CIA and other agencies had limited its access to the full record.

At the agencies' request the committee deleted three chapters from its report, one of them titled Budgetary Oversight. Among its findings were that congressional oversight had not been adequate and that Congress had failed to monitor intelligence expenditures; it recommended publishing the aggregate intelligence figure.

The committee documented that the CIA's covert mail programme, run by counterintelligence chief James Angleton from 1955 to 1973, was never processed through the Agency's approval system and had no separate funds; Angleton testified that normal processing would have opened the activity to too many people.

The total intelligence budget was disclosed for the first time in fifty years in 1997, $26.6 billion for FY1997, after FOIA litigation by the Federation of American Scientists; after the FY1998 figure disclosure stopped until the FY2007 figure.

The Rockefeller Commission disclosed in 1975, without naming him, the death of an Army employee given LSD without his knowledge in 1953; Congress compensated Frank Olson's family by Private Law 94-126, and President Ford, signing it on 12 October 1976, said his administration had supported a larger sum.

On 24 July 1986 GAO told a House Energy and Commerce subcommittee that Lockheed had reported 1,460 discrepancies in about 40,000 secret and top-secret items on a special access contract, with 11 unresolved, and that DoD had excluded special access programmes from Defense Investigative Service supervision in 1965. GAO called it inconsistent to create such a programme for security reasons and then give it less document protection.

In 1988 GAO reported to the defense committees under a statutory requirement that DoD did not adequately follow its criteria for creating special access programmes, and that the official required to keep a list of all of them did not do so.

At Schiff's request GAO searched from March 1994 to June 1995 and reported on 28 July 1995 that Roswell Army Air Field administrative records and outgoing messages for the late 1940s had been destroyed, that the disposition form does not say who destroyed them, when or under what authority, and that its search yielded two records originating in 1947.

The Air Force's Roswell reports state that they were produced in response to Schiff's inquiry; the 1994 report attributed the debris to a Project MOGUL balloon train and acknowledged that the 1947 weather balloon explanation was a cover story, and the 1997 report concluded the material was not an extraterrestrial spacecraft.

The Clinton Library holds correspondence between President Clinton and Laurance Rockefeller, photographs of the Clintons at Rockefeller's JY Ranch on 21 August 1995, and a White House Roswell file containing the July 1995 GAO report.

claimed.text: According to initiative participants, Rockefeller funded and directed a 1993 to 1996 effort to obtain presidential declassification, working through the White House science adviser's office, and its briefing document, The Best Available Evidence, compiled under Marie Galbraith with Stanton Friedman and Don Berliner, was distributed in 1995 to legislators, officials and heads of state.

Podesta publicly called for declassification of UFO records at a National Press Club event in October 2002, and on leaving the Obama White House in 2015 said his biggest failure of the year was once again not securing disclosure of the UFO files.
Michael Shellenberger and Mick West, who agree on little else, each name the Church Committee as the model for oversight of a compartmented programme.

Olson's sons alleged in a 2012 suit that his death was a murder concealed for sixty years; the District of Columbia court dismissed it in 2013 on timeliness, the 1976 waiver and sovereign immunity, while noting that the public record supports many of the allegations.

contested.text: The 1947 record GAO found is itself an explanation: an FBI teletype recorded an Eighth Air Force official describing a hexagonal disc suspended from a balloon that resembled a high-altitude weather balloon with a radar reflector. The CIA told GAO its databases held no documents on the crash.

The 1997 Air Force report attributes accounts of bodies to test dummies from parachute tests run mainly between 1953 and 1959; on the board's reading that reconstruction is weaker than the one it replaced.

A National Academy of Sciences panel concluded that extraterrestrial visitation was the least likely explanation and that UFO investigation warranted no high priority. The board infers that the 1966 pressure produced a contracted study that became the instrument of termination.
The Lockheed figures GAO gave in 1986 were Lockheed's reported results, which GAO said it had not yet verified, and GAO agreed not to identify the programme as a condition of access.

The opened Olson records disagree on the floor, the date of death and whether anyone was reprimanded: the Rockefeller Commission says two CIA employees were reprimanded, and the 2012 complaint says no formal reprimands were issued.
The board infers that neither the 1966 hearing nor the 1968 symposium produced any statute, records requirement or continuing oversight mechanism.

questions: What did Ford's March 1966 letters to the committee chairmen say, and why did the hearing last only a day?
Why did the 1968 symposium, with its scientific witnesses, lead to no legislation?
What was in the Church Committee's deleted Budgetary Oversight chapter?
Which programme was the Lockheed special access contract GAO examined in 1986?
Who destroyed the Roswell Army Air Field records, when and under what authority, and has any review ever answered GAO's finding?
What did Rockefeller say to Clinton at the JY Ranch in August 1995, and why did the initiative produce no declassification?
